name: a(n) is the maximum size of a subset S of {1,...,n} such that there are no solutions to 1/a = 1/b + 1/c for distinct a,b,c in S.
comment: Erdős has conjectured that a(n) = (1/2 + o(1))*n.
Further estimates can be found on the Erdős Problems site.
link: Sharvil Kesarwani, Table of n, a(n) for n = 1..731 (first 658 terms from Chai Wah Wu)
P. Erdős and R. Graham, Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory, Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
Erdős problems database contributors, Issue #152 linking Erdős problems to the OEIS.
Eric Weisstein's World of Mathematics, Erdős Problems.
example: For n = 12, the largest subset of {1,...,12} not containing the subsets {2, 3, 6}, {3, 4, 12}, {4, 12, 6} has size 10.
